title: Fix INT8 kernel auto-selector falling back to FP16 for specific shapes
author: Yuki Sato
release_notes:
- Fix INT8 kernel auto-selection for a shape class that previously fell back to FP16 (perf regression + confusing attribution).
- Add unit test coverage for INT8 selector invariants (no FP16 fallback unless explicitly allowed).
description:
Context: During the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint we saw a cluster of INT8 runs where throughput/TPOT matched FP16 behavior and kernel timelines showed FP16 GEMMs. Root cause was the kernel auto-selector treating some INT8 requests as "no matching INT8 kernel" (shape gating) and then silently falling back to FP16 even when quant_mode=INT8. This is both a performance regression (wasted quantization prep + worse cost-per-token) and makes profiling/attribution noisy.

What this PR does: (1) Adds a guard in the selector so that FP16 fallback is disallowed for quant_mode=INT8 unless the caller explicitly sets allow_fp16_fallback=true (only intended for emergency/bring-up). (2) Fixes the shape gating logic for INT8 GEMM candidates so that the affected shape family (notably large-N decode GEMMs with K aligned but M small and group_size=128) selects the expected INT8 kernel entry rather than returning "no match". (3) Adds a focused unit test that reproduces the failing shape and asserts the selected kernel family is INT8 (and that the selector does not emit FP16 when quant_mode=INT8).

Why now: This was implicated in SUP-6193 (customer-reported latency regression on INT8 variant after runtime update) and also showed up in the sprint matrix on A100/H100 when running mixed prompt-length workloads (decode-heavy). The change is intentionally conservative: it only tightens fallback behavior for INT8 and corrects a specific gating check; it does not change kernel implementations.

Testing: New unit tests under //runtime/tests cover the selector invariant and the regression shape. Existing runtime kernel selector tests pass. I also verified locally using the benchmark-lab reproduction config from the sprint matrix (INT8, streaming chat) and confirmed kernel selection is stable and throughput returns to expected INT8 baseline.

Rollout/Safety: The fallback guard preserves an explicit escape hatch (allow_fp16_fallback) for controlled experiments; default remains false in production configs. No public API changes.
commits: runtime/kernels: tighten INT8 selection invariants; prevent implicit FP16 fallback
runtime/kernels: fix INT8 candidate gating for small-M / large-N decode shapes
tests: add selector regression test covering failing INT8 shape
chore: add debug string for mismatch reason in selector unit test output
snippets:
Change summary (quant_kernel_selector.cc):
- if (req.quant_mode == QuantMode::INT8 && !req.allow_fp16_fallback) { disallow FP16 family candidates }
- fixed gating: treat (M <= 4) decode GEMMs as valid for INT8 catalog when K alignment satisfied; previously filtered by an overly strict M-tile constraint intended for a different kernel family

New test (quant_kernel_selector_test.cc):
- constructs request: quant_mode=INT8, group_size=128, dtype=INT8 weights, shape representative of decode step (M=1, N=8192, K=14336)
- asserts selected_kernel.family == INT8
- asserts selection fails fast (returns error) rather than silently picking FP16 when allow_fp16_fallback=false
conversation: Hiro Tanaka (review): Can you clarify whether we want to hard-error or soft-fallback when INT8 has no match? I agree silent FP16 is bad, but I want to ensure we don't turn transient catalog gaps into outages.

Yuki Sato (author): Good call. This PR keeps behavior as: INT8 + no match => error *unless* allow_fp16_fallback=true. In production we should treat "no INT8 match" as misconfig/bug and fail closed; for experiments/bring-up the escape hatch remains. I added wording in the header comment and expanded the test to assert we error rather than silently FP16.

Isabella Rossi (review): Please add a regression test that would have caught this earlier, and include the exact shape that showed up in benchmark-lab. Also, can we emit a reason string when no match happens? It will help debugging future catalog gaps.

Yuki Sato (author): Added testdata/quant_selector_shapes.json with the benchmark-derived shape and a focused unit test. Also added a debug-only mismatch reason string that shows up in test failures; kept it out of the hot path in production builds.
Noah Patel (review): The gating change worries me a bit—are we sure we aren't enabling an INT8 kernel for a shape it doesn't support? Any evidence from microbench / correctness?

Yuki Sato (author): The prior constraint was mistakenly inherited from an FP16 tile heuristic and was filtering valid INT8 catalog entries. I validated with the INT8 correctness test suite (existing) plus a targeted numeric drift check (INT8 vs FP16 baseline) for the same prompt set used in the sprint; no deltas beyond existing thresholds. Microbench shows expected INT8 kernel is selected and performance improves vs FP16 fallback.
Hiro Tanaka (review): Approved if CI green. Please also reference SUP-6193 in the PR description for release tracking.
Yuki Sato (author): Added SUP-6193 link and a release note bullet.
